item.title: Protesters ejected from raucous Trump rally in Texas
item.description: Several hecklers were removed from President Trump's rally in Texas late Wednesday, drawing jeers from the crowd as the president made fun of the protesters.

item.title: Oil prices surge as Trump reportedly mulls pre-midterms strikes on Iran
item.description: Crude oil prices spike again as The Atlantic reports Trump is considering new attacks on Iran before the U.S. midterms and fighting in Yemen intensifies.

item.title: Attorney for accused student in Cornell rape case speaks out
item.description: The attorney for one of the seven Cornell students accused of sexually assaulting a woman at a fraternity house in 2024 is speaking out. CBS News' Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: See the moment a police dog found a missing boy in the Maryland woods
item.description: A K-9 bloodhound named Beau helped rescue a missing boy in the Maryland woods after an hourslong search. Police body camera shows the storybook ending. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Christa Pike has pneumonia, unable to move arms after botched execution
item.description: Attorneys for Christa Pike, the Tennessee inmate who survived two doses of a lethal injection during her botched execution last week, shared an update on her health condition.

item.title: Iowa is grappling with Trump's economic policies despite being a reliably Republican state
item.description: Iowa voters are dealing with the impact of the current U.S. economy and may cast their votes seeking to distance themselves from President Trump. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Isaias becomes first hurricane of 2026 Atlantic season, threatens Gulf Coast
item.description: Hurricane Isaias developed late Wednesday as the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, taking aim at the Gulf Coast from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: U.S. service member describes low ammunition at Kuwait base, says Iran "hit us bad"
item.description: Newly obtained video shows an Iranian drone over Camp Buehring, a U.S. military base in Kuwait, before slamming into a building and causing an explosion. Jonah Kaplan has more.

item.title: Houthis claim they struck Riyadh's main airport in Saudi Arabia
item.description: Houthi rebels are claiming they attacked Saudi Arabia's main airport in Riyadh. Semafor Gulf's Mohammed Sergie breaks down whether this signals a full-blown regional war in the Middle East.

item.title: Trump approves nearly $18 million in disaster relief for Wisconsin towns desperate for tornado aid
item.description: President Trump approved nearly $18 million in FEMA disaster assistance for Wisconsin counties that got slammed by tornadoes back in July. Dr. Jon LaPook, who recently reported out of Menasha on the residents waiting for relief, joins with more.

item.title: Lab where Russian worker died suspected of previously developing bioweapons
item.description: The lab in Irkutsk, where the Russian worker died, has long been suspected of developing bioweapons, according to author Annie Jacobsen, who recently released her nonfiction book, "Biological War: A Scenario." Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Iowa trucker says Iran war, fuel prices have been "major struggle"
item.description: Some Iowans are questioning their loyalty to President Trump ahead of the midterms, saying they're struggling with the Iran war and tariffs. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Gillio Lopes' lawyer denies sexual assault claims in Cornell case
item.description: Gillio Lopes, one of the Chi Phi fraternity brothers accused of sexually assaulting Jane Doe in 2024, is denying the allegations. His lawyer, Andrew Miltenberg, told Lilia Luciano that his client's punishment of a suspension and essay was "unfair."

item.title: Ithaca council passes moratorium on new Cornell events permits
item.description: The mayor proposed the moratorium on campus events in the wake of a civil lawsuit filed last month​ by a former Cornell student who alleged she was drugged and gang-raped in 2024.

item.title: U.K. police release 7th man arrested over RAF Fairford incident on bail
item.description: All seven men arrested in the investigation, each in their 20s, now remain on police bail while "specialist teams continue to pursue all lines of enquiry," police said.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias intensifies and threatens parts of Mississippi, Alabama and Florida
item.description: Isaias has become the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season. It's currently aiming at the Florida Panhandle and parts of Mississippi and Alabama. CBS News' Rob Marciano reports.

item.title: Christa Pike's attorney shares details on her condition
item.description: Christa Pike's lawyer shared details on her condition Wednesday after she regained consciousness following two lethal doses of pentobarbital. Meanwhile, the botched execution is raising concerns about the drug. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Millions brace for Hurricane Isaias to make landfall
item.description: Millions of people are bracing for Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast. Rob Marciano has the latest.

item.title: Trump blasts Talarico in Texas and reverses comments on Iran bombing LA, San Diego
item.description: President Trump joined a rally in Texas for Ken Paxton's campaign, where he slammed Democratic candidate James Talarico. CBS News' Kathryn Watson reports.

item.title: Eye Opener: Millions brace for Hurricane Isaias
item.description: Millions of people along the Gulf Coast are preparing for Hurricane Isaias to make landfall. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Alleged Chinese agent to remain in custody, judge rules, amid flight-risk fears
item.description: California realtor Wanying Zhang is facing federal prosecution for allegedly surveilling the Taiwanese president's son in Washington last year at the direction of Chinese government officials.

item.title: Do You Have What It Takes to Be an Influencer? | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Everyone wants to ditch corporate America for the content creator lifestyle these days... but it may not be as easy as it sounds. Jill and Mark break down the pros and cons of the creator economy — and all the ups and downs that come with it. Plus, what's all this drama about iced coffee in job interviews? Jill and Mark have the scoop — and lots more to say about corporate etiquette.

item.title: FDA says its abortion pill safety review will continue into next year
item.description: The FDA says its ongoing safety review​ of the nation's main abortion pill​ will continue into next year, a timeline quickly condemned by abortion rights foes hoping to see the drug's use curtailed.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico due back in court to fight White House ban
item.description: Lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico will be back in court as the legal battle continues over President Trump's decision to ban their reporters from the White House.

item.title: Fears about kids' online safety unite Democrats and Republicans
item.description: Amid a decline in youth mental health, momentum is building for a federal crackdown on social media companies over protections for kids.

item.title: Newly obtained footage shows Iran attack on major U.S. post in Kuwait
item.description: CBS News obtained new video from a person on the ground showing an Iranian attack on a U.S. base at the beginning of the war.

item.title: Russia open to a Trump-Putin call as questions mount over plague lab death
item.description: Russia says it's open to a Trump-Putin phone call as concern and questions mount over a woman's death of "pneumonia of unknown origin."

item.title: "America's Startup" competitors use AI to launch businesses from their dorms
item.description: Young entrepreneurs are tapping AI to launch a range of businesses, from analyzing your skin to helping wine growers analyze crop yields.

item.title: JD Vance to speak with Tony Dokoupil for town hall ahead of midterms
item.description: Vice President JD Vance sits down with Tony Dokoupil this month to discuss the midterm elections and the issues shaping voters' choices, with questions from a live audience of Michigan voters.

item.title: CLEAR announces partnership with Veterans Affairs
item.description: CLEAR has expanded its reach beyond airports to healthcare, sports venues, workplaces and more. CLEAR chair and CEO Caryn Seidman Becker announces a new partnership with Veterans Affairs that's designed to make it easier for veterans to verify their identity and access benefits. Learn more (Sponsored by CLEAR)
